executive_summary: The run is at publishable-pending-owner-approval: the packet shows both proof-layout gates passing across 902 proof-bearing items, complete and exact judge coverage for the configured set at the frozen context, empty deferral lists, and zero workflow-owned blockers. The frontier spans 100 pages and 911 items across ten categories, dominated by the representation-theory-adjacent pages, and its historical fatal-defect record of 984 rows reads as churn rather than open risk: rows were fixed or superseded through 3a adjudication, owner repairs, and a final Step-5 adjudication wave whose per-row notes document the applied corrections. What remains is owner-side only — the personal mathematical audit, the deliberate status:published change, and push/deployment. Because judging is single-set and closure is bound to a frozen content hash, the audit is the last substantive mathematical check; the evidence points to the confirmed-fatal adjudication cohort and the twice-repaired items as the places to start, with claim-class and citation-class defects as the next target.
caveats: A cohort of Step-5 final-adjudication rows (the confirmed-fatal outcomes) keeps the ledger disposition 'deferred' rather than 'fixed' even though each such row carries an adjudicator note describing the correction that was applied; the packet's deferral lists are empty and the named closure artifact reports no open fatal items, so they read as recorded closures — but the label difference from the ordinary 'fixed' path is exactly why they deserve a direct read before publication.

The packet's repeated-repairs section lists items repaired twice; a second listed repair means an earlier fix was superseded or a late downstream effect surfaced, so a clean current diff does not by itself show that such an item is stable.

Judge coverage is complete, exact, and uniform (no null, incomplete, or mixed-set versions), but it rests on one configured judge set recorded against one frozen context; there is no independent second read, so the owner's personal audit is the only remaining mathematical cross-check.

Closure is bound to a frozen content hash and was verified against the current context; any content edit made after the audit invalidates the judge evidence for the changed items, so last-minute corrections must re-enter the workflow rather than be hand-edited.

Four category pathway briefs were rewritten and closed at the pathway stage, three of them with mechanical page-list repairs to frontmatter; this reader-facing navigation prose sits outside item-level verification.

owner_reading_priorities.subject: The confirmed-fatal Step-5 adjudication cohort — ledger rows labelled 'deferred' whose notes document the exact corrections applied.
owner_reading_priorities.reason: These are the run's last substantive edits, touching statements, definitions, proof steps, and fact blocks; reading each note against the item text is the fastest way to confirm the final correction wave landed as recorded.

owner_reading_priorities.subject: The twice-repaired items listed in the packet's repeated-repairs section.
owner_reading_priorities.reason: Double repair is the packet's own recurrence signal: a fix that needed reworking is where a residual mismatch between title, statement, facts block, and proof is most plausible.

owner_reading_priorities.subject: Items whose historical defects were claim-class or citation-class (overstrong statements and titles; inaccurate, inflated, missing, or misattributed citations).
owner_reading_priorities.reason: Layout gates cannot see these defects and judge context is frozen, so the exact strength of claims and fidelity to sources are settled only by owner-level reading of the statements and the cited works.

owner_reading_priorities.subject: The four rewritten category pathway briefs (complex-analysis, differential-geometry, representation-theory, special-topics-in-representation-theory).
owner_reading_priorities.reason: Page navigation was rewritten and, in three parts, mechanically repaired at closure; a rendered-page skim confirms the thematic arcs and page order still match the shipped items.

recommendations.recommendation: Begin the personal mathematical audit with the confirmed-fatal adjudication cohort: read each 'deferred' row's note, then confirm the described correction is present and mathematically sound in the item, routing any mismatch through the engine before publication.
recommendations.impact: Validates the run's last and least independently re-read correction wave at the locations — statements, definitions, proof steps, fact blocks — where an error would be most visible to readers.
recommendations.evidence: The packet's judges.adjudications records confirmed-fatal and confirmed-nonfatal outcomes with per-row correction notes; its deferral lists are empty and the named closure artifact reports no open fatal rows with closed true.

recommendations.recommendation: Then read the twice-repaired items and a sample of the claim-class and citation-class hotspots, and for each sampled citation repair read the exact cited statement in the source.
recommendations.impact: Covers the residual-risk classes that gates and frozen-context judging cannot settle: inference direction and hypothesis scope, claim strength in titles and statements, and source fidelity of citations.
recommendations.evidence: The packet's defect aggregates concentrate in inference- and claim-type subclasses and in statement, facts-block, definition, and proof-step locations, and its citation subclasses include inaccurate, inflated, missing, and misattributed entries.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep the status:published flip and push a pure state change: make no hand edits while flipping, and route any audit finding back through the engine's repair path so judging and layout gates refresh for the changed items.
recommendations.impact: Preserves the frozen judge evidence and hash binding through publication; a direct post-closure edit would silently invalidate the verdicts for the changed items.
recommendations.evidence: Readiness binds a frozen content hash and lists only the audit, status changes, and push as remaining actions; verification records complete exact verdicts for that context, and standing rules treat material rewrites as invalidating prior judge records.

recommendations.recommendation: Immediately before the flip, re-confirm that the working tree matches the audited frozen content hash so that nothing written after the audit rides along into the published state.
recommendations.impact: Catches accidental or drive-by edits that would otherwise publish unaudited content while the closure artifacts still claim complete coverage.
recommendations.evidence: The readiness artifact carries the frozen content hash, and the evidence packet's verification section records the run as verified against the current context at build time.

recommendations.recommendation: As the last non-item check, skim the four rewritten pathway brief sections and the rendered page order of the parts whose page lists were mechanically repaired.
recommendations.impact: Confirms reader-facing navigation prose and page order still match the shipped item sets after the late mechanical repairs.
recommendations.evidence: The pathway-closure artifact records four rewritten and closed briefs, with mechanical page-list repairs noted for the differential-geometry, representation-theory, and special-topics parts.
